title: "Create a new Vault" windows grouped in task manager are labeled "kded"
line: Vault dialogs now show up in the task manager as "Vaults" with the vault icon instead of being grouped under "KDED".
explanation: The vault dialogs (create, import, configure, unlock) are created by the plasmavault module inside kded6. On Wayland Qt sets every window's app id from the process's desktop file name when the window is shown, so they got kded's app id and the task manager grouped and labelled them as KDED. The change temporarily sets the desktop file name to org.kde.plasmavault while showing each vault dialog, and installs a hidden org.kde.plasmavault.desktop (Name Vaults, plasmavault icon, no Exec, like kded's own) so the task manager can name them.

commits.message:
kded: give the vault dialogs their own app id

The vault dialogs are windows of kded, so on Wayland they got its app id
and the task manager grouped them as "KDED" with its icon. Show them with
a Vaults app id and install a matching hidden desktop file for it.

BUG: 418011

media.caption: Master: three Create a New Vault dialogs grouped under the KDED icon, tooltip titled KDED
With the fix: the same three dialogs are grouped under the vault icon, tooltip titled Vaults

reviews.text: Pragmatic and minimal Wayland fix for vault dialogs being grouped under KDED: installing a hidden org.kde.plasmavault.desktop (mirroring kded's own) and temporarily setting QGuiApplication::desktopFileName() around show()/open() avoids a disruptive out-of-process IPC/security refactor while cleanly giving all four vault dialogs the Vaults app ID, titlebar icon, and task manager grouping. Restoring the previous desktopFileName immediately after synchronous show/open keeps other kded windows unaffected, and the before/after screenshots verify the result.
